# CheckboxGroup

A group of checkboxes under one legend, on the Field contract, for picking any number of choices: pass `legend`, and `options` (or `Checkbox` children). `value` is the list of checked values; with `name`, each checked box submits `name=value` with its form. `error` and `required` apply to the whole group.

```tsx
import { CheckboxGroup } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/checkbox/checkbox-group";
```

## Example

```tsx
<CheckboxGroup
  legend="Herbs"
  name="herbs"
  defaultValue={["basil"]}
  options={[
    { value: "basil", label: "Basil", description: "Sweet and peppery." },
    { value: "mint", label: "Mint" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `RadioGroup` instead when exactly one choice may be picked, `Checkbox` for a single yes-or-no choice, and `Fieldset` to group different fields.

## Props

Props every mode takes. Type: `CheckboxGroupProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-4`, `col-span-2`). Appearance classes warn in development; style checkboxes in your theme. |
| `defaultValue` | `string[]` |  | The values checked at first, for an uncontrolled group. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Supporting text under the legend, read after it through `aria-describedby`. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Disables every box and fades the group. |
| `error` | `string \| string[]` |  | What is wrong, from your server action or client check, shown under the choices; every box gets `aria-invalid`. An empty string or array means valid. |
| `hideLegend` | `boolean` |  | Hides the legend visually; screen readers still read it as the group's name. |
| `legend` (required) | `string` |  | What the group is, shown above the choices and read as the group's name. Required: a group of controls needs a name. To hide it visually, keep it and add `hideLegend`. |
| `name` | `string` |  | The form field name every checked box submits under, once per checked value. |
| `onValueChange` | `((value: string[]) => void)` |  | Called with every checked value, in the order they were checked, when one is checked or unchecked. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | The group element, a `<div role="group">`. |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | At least one box must be checked to submit the form: the legend gets a marker, and the browser shows `requiredMessage` until one is checked. |
| `requiredMessage` | `string` | `"Choose at least one."` | What the browser says when `required` and nothing is checked. Translate it here. |
| `value` | `string[]` |  | The checked values, for a controlled group; pair it with `onValueChange`. |

## Modes

`CheckboxGroupProps` is a union: pass the props of exactly one mode. Mixing them is a type error.

### With `children`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | The choices as `Checkbox` elements, each with a `value`, for a layout `options` cannot express. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `options`: Not with children: pass the choices one way.

### With `options`

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (required) | `CheckboxGroupOption[]` |  | The choices, one box each, in order. |

Not in this mode (typed `never`):

- `children`: Not with `options`: pass the choices one way.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `errorMessage`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `error`: `<CheckboxGroup error="Required.">`.
- `helperText`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `description`: `<CheckboxGroup description="...">`.
- `invalid`: Not a prop. `error` marks the group invalid: `<CheckboxGroup error="What is wrong">`.
- `isDisabled`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `disabled`: `<CheckboxGroup disabled>`.
- `isInvalid`: Not a prop. `error` marks the group invalid: `<CheckboxGroup error="What is wrong">`.
- `isRequired`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `required`: `<CheckboxGroup required>`.
- `items`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `options`: `options={[{ value: "basil", label: "Basil" }]}`.
- `label`: Not a prop. A group is named by its `legend`: `<CheckboxGroup legend="Herbs">`.
- `onChange`: Not a prop. Ouro UI uses `onValueChange`, which gets the checked values: `onValueChange={setValues}`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: each component merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with the component's own replaces it.

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `CheckboxGroupOption`

One choice in a `CheckboxGroup`'s `options`.

```ts
interface CheckboxGroupOption {
  /** What the box submits, and its entry in the group's `value`. */
  value: string;
  /** The choice's name, shown to the right of its box. */
  label: string;
  /** Supporting text under the label, read after it. */
  description?: ReactNode | undefined;
  /** Disables this one box. */
  disabled?: boolean | undefined;
}
```
